a:r.a:t: Amino Acids Does Not Occur in the Liver
Leucine, isoleucine, and valine are oxidized for fuel.
In muscle, adipose tissue, the kidneys, and the brain

p:cNvPr.descr: An image depicting catabolic pathways for the three branched-chain amino acids: valine, isoleucine, and leucine. At the top left is valine, where C bonds left to H3N (plus sign over N), up to COO-, right to H and down to CH, which bonds left to CH3 and down to CH3. Below this is isoleucine, which begins with C. C bonds left to H3N (plus sign over N), up to COO-, right to H and down to CH, which bonds left to CH3 and down to CH2, which bonds down to CH3. Below this is leucine, which begins with C. C bonds left to H3N (plus sign over N), up to COO-, right to H, and down to CH2, which bonds down to CH, which bonds left to CH3 and down to CH3. To the right top, C bonds up to COO-, double bonds right to O and down to CH, which bonds left to CH3 and down to CH3. Below this is C bonding up to COO-, double bonding right to O and bonding down to CH, which bonds left to CH3 and down to CH2, which bonds down to CH3. Below this is C, which bonds up to COO-, double bonds right to O and bonds down to CH2, which bonds down to CH, which bonds left to CH3 and down to CH3. These are all alpha-keto acids. There is an arrow pointing from valine down and right, then right, the up and right to the first alpha-keto acid. Below this is another arrow pointing right to alpha-keto acids. From leucine is another arrow pointing up and right, the right, then down and right to the third alpha-keto acid. This arrow has branched-chain aminotransferase (in blue) below it. In the third column are Acyl-CoA derivatives. At the top C double bonds up and left to O, up and right to S-CoA and down to CH, which bonds left to CH3 and down to CH3. Below this is C, which double bonds up and left to O, up and right to S-CoA and down to CH, which bonds left to CH3 and down to CH2, which bonds down to CH3. Below this is C double bonding up and left to O, bonding up and right to S-CoA and down to CH2, which bonds down to CH, which bonds left to CH3 and down to CH3. An arrow points from the first alpha-keto acid down and right, then right, then up and right to the first Acyl-CoA derivative. An arrow below this points right from alpha-keto acids to Acyl-CoA derivatives. The third alpha-keto acid has an arrow pointing up and right, then right, then down and right to the third Acyl-CoA derivatives. This arrow has branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex (in blue) below. Below this is a red X in a red circle, with a red arrow pointing down to maple syrup urine disease in a tan box. The top arrow has three curved arrows. All point from CoA-SH to CO2. The first dips to the first arrow and has NAD in the arc. The second dips to the straight arrow pointing from alpha-keto acids to Acyl-CoA derivatives. The last arrow dips to the bottom arrow.
